note: TWO FLYOUTS WERE OPEN AT ONCE, AND THE PANEL TOOK CLICKUP'S SHAPE. The founder's screenshot of the desktop rail showed the CONTENT flyout AND the MINISTRY flyout rendered simultaneously, overlapping, with CONTENT's single row clipped under MINISTRY's panel — 'it looks so ugly', but the appearance was the symptom. The cause was that THE-332 gave every NavRailFlyout its OWN open/pinned state, four instances with nothing coordinating them, and the pin was explicitly allowed to survive a hover-close, so a pressed CONTENT stayed up while a hovered MINISTRY opened beside it. THE-334 lifts the open group into ONE `openGroup: string | null` held by NavRailProvider, so opening one closes the others BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by four components racing; Base UI ships no coordination primitive for sibling popovers (its popover exports root, trigger, positioner, popup, portal, arrow, backdrop, title, description, close and viewport, and nothing that groups two roots), which is why the state is lifted rather than delegated. It then gives the panel the shape the founder specified from a ClickUp reference: visible short text labels under the rail icons, a full-height floating panel, a real Base UI arrow pointing out of the selected rail entry, a title row, a body sectioned with separators inside a scroll-area, and a pinned footer holding the group's recent items. Settings LEAVES the rail for the account menu now pinned at the rail's floor, at the founder's explicit instruction, behind the same `canSettings` entitlement it always carried. MOBILE IS UNTOUCHED: MORE_GROUPS, the bottom nav and the More sheet are unchanged, as are firestore.rules, firestore.indexes.json, functions/ and layout.tsx. No npm dependency was added, no theme token was minted, and all 43 installed primitives are byte-identical.

entries.why: THE COORDINATION, AND THE PANEL'S SHAPE. `NavRailProvider` holds one `openGroup` for all four flyouts and `NavRailFlyout` READS it instead of owning it, so no state exists in which two panels are open — restoring per-instance state is what THE-334's test 1 and test 2 fail on, verified by planting exactly that defect. `openGroup` REPLACES the whole state rather than merging, so a press-pinned CONTENT cannot survive MINISTRY opening; `closeGroup` ignores a STALE close from a group that is no longer the open one (or hovering the next group would blank the panel that just opened) and lets a pin survive the POINTER LEAVING and nothing else — Escape, an outside press, focus-out and a second press all arrive with a different reason and each both closes AND unpins. `sheet` was REJECTED for the full-height panel even though it is edge-anchored and full-height by design, because it is Base UI's DIALOG: `Dialog.Trigger` has no `openOnHover` at all, so hover could only return as the hand-rolled pointer listeners Popover exists to make unnecessary, and `SheetContent` mounts a backdrop that would make the nav modal. `PopoverContent` was replaced by the Base UI parts one level down — Portal / Positioner / Popup / Arrow — because it hardcodes its own Positioner (no `anchor`, no arrow slot) and `src/components/ui/popover.tsx` is DIGEST-PINNED byte-for-byte by THE-308's guard, so it could not be extended; `Popover` and `PopoverTrigger` are still the repo's own wrappers. The ARROW is Base UI's own part, not a drawn triangle, anchored to the trigger so it points out of the rail entry the panel belongs to; `ui/popover.tsx` does not re-export it, which is reported as this ticket's STOP 6c. Full height is the viewport's own height less the collision padding, settled by the positioner's default alignment shift, so this file computes no coordinate. The WIDTH is untouched at `w-64` — sidebar.tsx's own SIDEBAR_WIDTH — and the hover gate, its three conditions and its false-first effect are byte-identical in behaviour. It hardcodes no colour, renders no emoji and adds no dependency.

GAINED `DESKTOP_GROUP_LABELS`, and nothing else — the icon map above it is untouched. The rail's labels are VISIBLE TEXT now rather than `sr-only`, which is the founder's ask ('there's no title under to know what category is it') and what ClickUp's own rail does throughout. A SECOND map rather than a rename: the keys of DESKTOP_NAV_GROUPS are what seven pre-existing entitlement guards scan the nav by, so renaming MINISTRY to People in that array to fit the rail would have been a permission-shaped edit made for a typographic reason. The words were shortened rather than the rail widened — an 88px rail minus its padding leaves 56px of measure and BROADCASTING needs about 80px even at 10px type — and the founder chose the set himself (Home, Content, People, Live, Grow) when shown the three candidates, having also asked for the nav to be less wide. No word exceeds seven characters, so every label sits on one line at the rail's existing width. It holds no colour, no width and no permission logic.

NEW. The 'Recent' block pinned to the bottom of a flyout, which the founder asked for after seeing the shape ('also under the list show the recent things like in clickup. Latest notes, latest forms, latest etc'). It takes the pinned-footer slot because his reference's own footer is an AI credit meter he ruled out himself ('it's their AI, we don't have such thing yet'), so the footer holds real data instead of an invented usage meter. 🔴 IT ADDS NO FIRESTORE INDEX, AND THAT IS THE POINT: the obvious build is `orderBy('updatedAt').limit(5)` per collection, which needs a composite index, and `.github/workflows/deploy-rules.yml` triggers only on firestore.rules / storage.rules / firebase.json and runs `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules,storage` — it NEVER deploys `firestore:indexes`, so an index added there is INERT, the query fails, and useDocsQueries records that the failure is SILENT. The founder was shown this and chose the index-free path. Every source is a read the app already makes: useDocs is tenant-scoped with no orderBy and already returned updatedAt-descending, useContacts is that same read re-sorted with the shared sortByTime helper, useEvents is a single-field orderBy Firestore indexes automatically. It is a COMPONENT rather than a hook in the shell so that it mounts inside the popup and its read runs only when a panel is actually opened. GROW gets no footer because it has no per-item recency to show and a footer that invents one would be a footer that lies. It hardcodes no colour and renders no emoji.

THE RAIL IS FIVE ENTRIES AND AN AVATAR. The four flyouts are wrapped in NavRailProvider so they share one open group; each rail entry now draws its icon over a VISIBLE short label; and SETTINGS LEFT THE RAIL for the account menu pinned at the column's floor, at the founder's explicit instruction ('at the bottom of sidebar put the profile picture with its settings… remove the settings from the sidebar'). Nothing was lost and no gate moved: accountMenuProps.onOpenSettings already carried the SAME canSettings entitlement and already called go('settings'), so an admin without it still sees no Settings row anywhere, and THE-334's guard WALKS that path — it opens the avatar, finds the row, clicks it and requires the router to be sent to the settings URL — rather than excusing the id. `goItem` was added beside `go` so a recent note or person opens ON the thing picked, using the `:itemId` segment three screens already consume. `desktopSidebarGroups` and `visibleNavGroups` are untouched, so a group with no permitted tabs is still omitted whole and `library` is still isSuperAdmin-only. The rail column stays `lg:w-[88px]` and the content box still gets 144px back — no width is invented. Every mobile class, MORE_GROUPS, the More sheet, the top bar and every screen mount are unchanged. THE-327's colour-literal budget is unchanged: the new code reuses the existing RAIL_ACTIVE_INK constant and adds no literal.

GAINED ONE OPTIONAL `variant` PROP, defaulting to the behaviour every pre-existing caller already had. The menu is now also the rail's account entry, and on the rail two things change together because they are one decision: it opens UPWARD, because the avatar is pinned to the floor of a full-height column and a downward menu would open off the bottom of the viewport; and its trigger is `w-11 h-11` rather than `w-9 h-9`, because on the rail it is a NAV TARGET — the only path from the rail to Settings — rather than an identity affordance beside a row of other controls. That second half was MEASURED, not assumed: at 36px the avatar measured 32.6px on desktop, under Rule 4's own DENSITY_PX.control floor of 38, and at 44px it measures 39.875px, inside the band. The top bar's instance is untouched in both placement and size. The panel stays `w-60` and its rows stay `w-full`, so THE-181's guard on this file still holds, and no permission, no row and no handler changed.

GAINED A POLYFILL FOR `Element.getAnimations`, which happy-dom does not implement. Base UI's ScrollArea viewport calls it on every scroll-state effect, and in happy-dom the call THROWS — from inside an effect, so no assertion fails and no test goes red: vitest counts it as an unhandled error and the run EXITS 1 WITH EVERY TEST PASSING. That is the exact failure mode this repo already has one documented instance of (the stray sonner timer, card 86bbwjkvc), and introducing a second one while fixing a nav bug would have been a poor trade. It is fixed in the ENVIRONMENT rather than by avoiding the primitive, because scroll-area is what lets a nine-tab group scroll inside the full-height flyout and hand-rolling an overflow div to dodge a missing DOM method would trade a real primitive for a harness omission. It returns `[]`, which is what a real browser returns when nothing is animating — always true here, since happy-dom runs no animations at all. It is guarded on the method being absent, so a future environment that implements it keeps its own.
